chunks: From him, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

For one hand there is half of the diyah, and for both hands together there is the full diyah; and regarding the two feet likewise. And regarding the male organ, if the glans and what is beyond that is cut, there is the full diyah. And regarding the nose, if the soft protruding part is cut, there is the full diyah. And regarding the two lips there is the full diyah. And regarding the two eyes there is the full diyah, and for one of them there is half of the diyah.

key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: financial compensation due for bodily injury or killing
key_terms.الذَّكَرِ: the male organ in the context of injury compensation
key_terms.الشَّفَتَيْنِ: the two lips, for which full diyah is assigned here
key_terms.الْحَشَفَةُ: the glans of the male organ
key_terms.الْعَيْنَيْنِ: the two eyes, for which full diyah is assigned here
key_terms.الْمَارِنُ: the soft projecting part of the nose
key_terms.الْيَدَيْنِ: both hands together, carrying the full diyah
key_terms.الْيَدِ: a single hand, for which half the diyah is assigned here

ai.seo_question: What diyah is due for cutting off a hand, eye, nose, lips, or other body parts in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states fixed diyah compensations for the loss of specific body parts and paired limbs. It is a jurisprudential text used in discussions of bodily injury, compensation, and legal rights in cases of harm.
